clue.text: Massively significant audio books?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for something that says a great deal without words
second meaning, whimsical: recorded books are volumes that literally speak

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: an audiobook is a volume read aloud by a narrator.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a gesture or fact that is highly telling, conveying much meaning by itself.

clue.text: Artificial pond mostly clean

parts.note: a sham is a fake, something artificial

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pool is a small body of still water

explanation.surface: Someone is scrubbing out a man-made garden pond, getting it nearly clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To shampoo a carpet or hair is to wash it with a cleaning liquid, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Looking up, some admired leafy tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of these two words are used, running across the word break

parts.note: the run of letters is taken from inside these two words

explanation.surface: Someone gazes upward at a leafy tree they admire.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree or shrub bearing white flowers and dark berries, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Think I set cryptic to be playful?

indicators.note: something cryptic is puzzling and obscure, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A setter wonders whether writing a cryptic clue is a light-hearted, playful pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittenish describes lively, frisky, coquettish behaviour, like that of a young cat at play.

clue.text: Tebbit maybe missing final note in Bellini opera

indicators.note: n. is the abbreviation for a note, and the name here lacks that letter at its end

parts.note: Norman Tebbit was a Conservative cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher

explanation.surface: A politician is absent from the final scene of an opera by Bellini.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Tebbit was a prominent British Conservative politician of the 1980s; the maybe marks him as one example of a Norman.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Vincenzo Bellini's 1831 opera about a druid priestess, famous for the aria Casta diva.

clue.text: Grips five sorbets?

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
sorbets are water ices, frozen desserts

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is clutching five sorbets at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a workbench clamp that holds an object firmly, so the plural noun means grips or clamps.

clue.text: Going north, chaplain occasionally picked lake flower

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the letters are read upwards, back to front
only every other letter is selected from the word

parts.note: its first, third, fifth and seventh letters are used

explanation.surface: A chaplain walking north picks a flower beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom clusters, so it is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Drink with servant Brown when touring Balmoral?

indicators.note: the outer letters go around the inner ones, as a traveller goes round a place

parts.note: a man is a manservant
tan is a light brown colour
a balmoral is a flat Scottish cap, so a type of hat

explanation.surface: A servant called Brown goes for a drink while touring Balmoral Castle in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral looks like the royal castle in Scotland, but here it is the Scottish bonnet named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters, an example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: Shilling verily forged to appear thus!

definitions.text: Shilling verily forged to appear thus!

parts.note: S was the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money

indicators.note: forged means beaten into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A counterfeit shilling would need to look silvery to pass as real.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a fake shilling must appear silvery. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A forged coin would be made to have a shining grey sheen like real silver, which is what silvery means.

clue.text: Examiner's car, rubbish in reverse

definitions.note: read as Examiner is, the 's joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: the word is read backwards, as a car goes in reverse

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A driving examiner's car is a heap of rubbish when going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects and checks financial accounts, so is an official examiner of books.

clue.text: Rank marrow picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a kernel is the inner core or marrow of something

explanation.surface: A gardener picks up a fine marrow from the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: A marrow is also a large vegetable, the surface sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel is a military rank in the army, above lieutenant colonel and below brigadier.

clue.text: Funds get tighter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is money available, as in the public ...
second meaning: to ... the lips is to pucker or tighten them

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a squeeze on finances; the two meanings are a sum of money and the tightening of lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Purse names an amount of money such as prize money, and as a verb means to draw the lips together.

clue.text: Workmate's Hobnob

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colleague or partner at work
second meaning: to mix socially with someone

explanation.walkthrough: Hobnob looks like the British chocolate oat biscuit eaten at work; here it is the verb to socialise.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a business partner or colleague, and to associate with people is to spend time with them socially.

clue.text: Defiant expression of heavy drinker at home?

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here means in this place, where one lives

explanation.surface: A drunkard at home makes a defiant retort.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a childish retort used to assert one has won an argument, an idiom of defiance.

clue.text: One benefiting from hothouse, or young person left ignored?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter is passed over, so it drops out of the word

parts.note: a child is a young person

explanation.surface: A question of whether a hothouse helps a plant, or a neglected young person.
explanation.walkthrough: Hothousing also means intensive schooling of children, which the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are tropical plants that thrive in the warm, humid conditions of a greenhouse.

clue.text: Has lyrics rewritten for monarch-to-be, maybe

indicators.note: rewriting changes the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A song has new lyrics written for a future king's coronation.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch is a butterfly, not a royal; maybe marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysalis is the pupa stage from which a butterfly such as a monarch emerges.

clue.text: Records sample album by Carole King

parts.note: tapes are recordings
to sample is to try out

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sample from records by Carole King.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestry is Carole King's 1971 album, one of the best-selling records of its era.

clue.text: The Observer covering Labour leads to complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: the eye is the organ that observes
to strain is to labour or toil hard

explanation.surface: A newspaper's coverage of the Labour Party leads to a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer looks like the British Sunday newspaper; here it is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is fatigue or soreness of the eyes, a minor medical complaint.

clue.text: Moving around island, rare and shy farm animal

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rare, timid animal is moved around an island farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ayrshire is a breed of dairy cattle from south-west Scotland, so an example of a farm animal.

clue.text: Tornadoes here, or atmosphere fair?

parts.note: air is the atmosphere
a show is a fair or exhibition

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether tornadoes form here or whether the weather is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tornado is an RAF fighter jet, not a storm; such jets fly at airshows.
explanation.definitionFit: An airshow is a display of aircraft, where military jets such as Tornadoes perform.

clue.text: What could be broad and very large for social gatherings

parts.note: a broad bean is one kind of bean
OS is the clothing size outsize

explanation.surface: Large broad-minded parties suggest what could be broad and huge.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is a British informal word for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanos are noisy celebrations or parties, so they are social gatherings.

clue.text: Southern gentleman on crack, creating a situation

parts.note: he refers to a man
a crack is a loud sharp noise, a bang

explanation.surface: A Southern gentleman taking crack cocaine creates a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drugs; crack is the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang means an affair or state of things, as in the whole shebang.

clue.text: Perfume of drink that follows wine

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
water is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone smells the perfume of a drink taken after wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewater is a fragrant liquid distilled from rose petals, used as a scent and in cooking.

clue.text: Almost difficult at first fishing under wide pier

indicators.note: in a down clue the rest sits below the first piece
almost all of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of fishing is F

explanation.surface: Fishing off a wide pier is hard at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf is a landing place where ships moor to load, like a pier or quay.

clue.text: Upset boy, computers affected by current

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A boy is upset that computers are being affected by an electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal waters rise and fall with the tide, so they are subject to the current of the sea.

clue.text: Supervised church farm

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone supervised a farm owned by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in North America.

clue.text: Son visiting gallery for experience

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A son visits an art gallery for the experience.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to experience it briefly, as in a taste of freedom.

clue.text: Did butterfly possibly start to interest Hindu teacher?

parts.note: butterfly is a swimming stroke, so doing it means one swam

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of interest is I

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a butterfly sparked a Hindu teacher's interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Stop short in front of garden rope

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to halt is to stop
yard is the American word for a garden

explanation.surface: Someone halts just before reaching the garden rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A halyard is a rope used on a ship to raise or lower a sail or flag.

clue.text: Falls once more, looking back by regatta on vacation

indicators.note: one piece sits beside the next
the word is read backwards

parts.note: again means once more

indicators.note: the word is vacated, emptied of its middle letters

parts.note: only the outer letters of regatta survive once it is emptied

explanation.surface: Someone falls once more while looking back at a regatta on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is the famous waterfall on the border of Canada and the United States.

clue.text: Unrealistic expectations around Wells?

definitions.meaning: the plain sense: hoping for something unlikely
thinking about wells, as at a wishing well, where people toss coins and wish

explanation.walkthrough: Wells looks like the cathedral city in Somerset, or H. G. Wells; the question mark points to wishing wells.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means believing something because one wants it to be true, not because it is likely.
